scope: Genesis 32–36, all 155 public verses. Genesis 32:1–32 ET is Gen 32:2–33 HT; Gen 32:1 HT belongs to the preceding public verse. Prior revisions remain unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact UTF-8 <verse ...>...</verse> substring, including markup, whitespace, written forms, and any reading notes. No XML reserialization or Hebrew normalization.
source.public_versification_note: English Genesis 32:1–32 is bound to Hebrew Gen 32:2–33. Hebrew Gen 32:1 is already bound to English Genesis 31:55 in the preceding ledger. Numbering realigns at Genesis 33.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Use the familiar biblical term angels for God’s messengers and keep their unexplained encounter with Jacob concise.
verses.before: Jacob went on his way, and the angels of God met him.
verses.after: Jacob continued on his way, and God’s angels met him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jacob went on his way, and the angels of God met him.

verses.rationale: Preserve Jacob’s exclamation and the camp/Mahanaim name association without explaining what the angels do not say.
verses.before: When Jacob saw them, he said, “This is God’s camp.” So he called that place Mahanaim.
verses.after: When Jacob saw them, he said, “This is God’s camp!” So he named that place Mahanaim.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Jacob saw them, he said, “This is God’s camp.” So he called that place Mahanaim.

verses.rationale: Clarify that the second land phrase locates Seir while retaining Esau’s brotherhood and the Edom connection.
verses.before: Jacob sent messengers before him to his brother Esau in the land of Seir, the country of Edom,
verses.after: Jacob sent messengers ahead of him to his brother Esau in the land of Seir, the territory of Edom.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jacob sent messengers before him to his brother Esau in the land of Seir, the country of Edom,

verses.rationale: Render sojourn as resident-foreigner status and preserve Jacob’s repeated deferential lord/servant language.
verses.before: instructing them, “Thus you will say to my lord Esau: ‘Thus says your servant Jacob: I have sojourned with Laban and stayed until now;
verses.after: He commanded them, “Tell my lord Esau, ‘This is what your servant Jacob says: I have lived as a resident foreigner with Laban and remained there until now.
verses.tsw_comparator: instructing them, “Thus you shall say to my lord Esau: ‘Thus says your servant Jacob: I have sojourned with Laban and stayed until now;

verses.rationale: Preserve the property list and make the enslaved status of the gender-specific servants explicit; render favor-in-your-eyes naturally without promising Esau’s response.
verses.before: and I have oxen, donkeys, flocks, male servants, and female servants. I send to tell my lord, so that I may find favor in your sight.’”
verses.after: I now have cattle, donkeys, flocks, enslaved men, and enslaved women. I am sending this message to my lord in the hope that you will receive me favorably.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: and I have oxen, donkeys, flocks, male servants, and female servants. I send to tell my lord, in order that I may find favor in your sight.’”

verses.rationale: Make the messengers’ completed errand and the alarming approach clear while retaining brother and the exact number.
verses.before: The messengers returned to Jacob, saying, “We came to your brother Esau, and he is coming to meet you, and four hundred men are with him.”
verses.after: The messengers returned to Jacob and reported, “We went to your brother Esau. He is already coming to meet you, and four hundred men are with him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The messengers returned to Jacob, saying, “We came to your brother Esau, and he is coming to meet you, and four hundred men are with him.”

verses.rationale: Separate emotion from response for oral clarity and retain both fear and distress, every group, and the two-camp motif.
verses.before: Then Jacob was greatly afraid and distressed; and he divided the people who were with him, and the flocks and herds and camels, into two camps,
verses.after: Jacob became very afraid and distressed. He divided the people with him, along with the flocks, herds, and camels, into two camps.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Jacob was greatly afraid and distressed; and he divided the people who were with him, and the flocks and herds and camels, into two camps,

verses.rationale: Render the hypothetical violence and hoped-for escape directly without asserting Esau’s intent.
verses.before: thinking, “If Esau comes to the one camp and strikes it, then the camp that is left will escape.”
verses.after: He thought, “If Esau attacks one camp, the other camp may escape.”
verses.tsw_comparator: thinking, “If Esau comes to the one camp and strikes it, then the camp that is left will escape.”

verses.rationale: Identify Abraham’s actual relationship to Jacob while retaining the ancestral prayer formula, the divine name, command, and promise.
verses.before: Jacob said, “O God of my father Abraham and God of my father Isaac, O LORD who said to me, ‘Return to your country and to your kindred, and I will do you good,’
verses.after: Then Jacob prayed, “God of my grandfather Abraham and my father Isaac, LORD, you told me, ‘Return to your land and your family, and I will be good to you.’
verses.tsw_comparator: And Jacob said, “O God of my father Abraham and God of my father Isaac, O LORD who said to me, ‘Return to your country and to your kindred, and I will do you good,’

verses.rationale: Render Jacob’s smallness as unworthiness, preserve the paired covenant qualities, and clarify what became two camps without losing the staff-to-abundance contrast.
verses.before: I am not worthy of all the steadfast love and all the faithfulness that you have shown to your servant; for with only my staff I crossed this Jordan, and now I have become two camps.
verses.after: I am unworthy of all the faithful love and faithfulness you have shown your servant. I crossed this Jordan with only my staff, but now my household has become two camps.
verses.tsw_comparator: I am not worthy of all the steadfast love and all the faithfulness that you have shown to your servant; for with only my staff I crossed this Jordan, and now I have become two camps.

verses.rationale: Keep the repeated brother/Esau identification, Jacob’s admitted fear, and the source’s concrete image of wholesale destruction.
verses.before: Deliver me, I pray, from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau, for I fear him, that he may come and strike me, the mothers with the children.
verses.after: Please save me from my brother Esau. I am afraid he will come and strike me down, mothers along with their children.
verses.tsw_comparator: Deliver me, I pray, from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau, for I fear him, that he may come and strike me, the mothers with the children.

verses.rationale: Preserve the emphatic promise, offspring, sea-sand image, and uncountable multitude as Jacob’s appeal.
verses.before: Yet you said, ‘I will surely do you good, and make your offspring as the sand of the sea, which cannot be numbered for multitude.’”
verses.after: You yourself said, ‘I will surely be good to you and make your offspring like the sand of the sea, too numerous to count.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet you said, ‘I will surely do you good, and make your offspring as the sand of the sea, which cannot be numbered for multitude.’”

verses.rationale: Make the selection natural in English while keeping the night, available property, gift, and brother relationship.
verses.before: So he spent that night there. And from what he had with him he took a gift for his brother Esau:
verses.after: Jacob spent that night there. From the possessions at hand, he selected a gift for his brother Esau:
verses.tsw_comparator: So he spent that night there. And from what he had with him he took a gift for his brother Esau:

verses.rationale: Retain the clear existing enumeration because every species, sex, and number corresponds directly to the source.
verses.before: two hundred female goats and twenty male goats, two hundred ewes and twenty rams,
verses.after: two hundred female goats and twenty male goats, two hundred ewes and twenty rams,
verses.tsw_comparator: two hundred female goats and twenty male goats, two hundred ewes and twenty rams,

verses.rationale: Use nursing with their young for the maternal animals and retain every sex and exact number.
verses.before: thirty milking camels and their calves, forty cows and ten bulls, twenty female donkeys and ten male donkeys.
verses.after: thirty nursing camels with their young, forty cows and ten bulls, twenty female donkeys and ten male donkeys.
verses.tsw_comparator: thirty milking camels and their calves, forty cows and ten bulls, twenty female donkeys and ten male donkeys.

verses.rationale: Make the servants’ enslaved status visible, keep their entrusted task, and preserve the deliberate spacing of separate herds.
verses.before: These he handed over to his servants, every drove by itself, and said to his servants, “Pass on ahead of me, and put a space between drove and drove.”
verses.after: He entrusted each herd separately to his enslaved men and told them, “Go ahead of me, and leave some space between each herd.”
verses.tsw_comparator: These he handed over to his servants, every drove by itself, and said to his servants, “Pass on ahead of me, and put a space between drove and drove.”

verses.rationale: Clarify the leader of the first herd and turn the terse ownership questions into natural speech without changing their content.
verses.before: He instructed the foremost, “When Esau my brother meets you and asks you, ‘To whom do you belong? Where are you going? And whose are these ahead of you?’
verses.after: He instructed the one in front, “When my brother Esau meets you, he may ask, ‘Whose servant are you? Where are you going? Whose animals are these ahead of you?’
verses.tsw_comparator: He instructed the foremost, “When Esau my brother meets you and asks you, ‘To whom do you belong? Where are you going? And whose are these ahead of you?’

verses.rationale: Keep the lord/servant diplomacy, identify the gift’s owner, and make the final pronoun explicit.
verses.before: then you will say, ‘They belong to your servant Jacob; they are a gift sent to my lord Esau, and moreover he is behind us.’”
verses.after: Then answer, ‘They belong to your servant Jacob. This is a gift sent to my lord Esau, and Jacob himself is coming behind us.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: then you shall say, ‘They belong to your servant Jacob; they are a gift sent to my lord Esau, and moreover he is behind us.’”

verses.rationale: Preserve the repeated staged instructions and the second, third, and all-following sequence.
verses.before: He likewise instructed the second and the third, and everyone who followed the droves, “You will say the same thing to Esau when you meet him,
verses.after: Jacob gave the same command to the second and third servants and to everyone following the herds: “Say these same words to Esau when you meet him.
verses.tsw_comparator: He likewise instructed the second and the third, and all who followed the droves, “You shall say the same thing to Esau when you meet him,

verses.rationale: Retain Jacob’s strategy and uncertainty; keep one face expression in the text and disclose the source’s denser face wordplay in a note.
verses.before: and you will say, ‘Moreover your servant Jacob is behind us.’” For he thought, “I may appease him with the gift that goes ahead of me, and afterward I will see his face; perhaps he will accept me.”
verses.after: Be sure to say, ‘Your servant Jacob is coming behind us.’” Jacob thought, “I will appease Esau with the gift going ahead of me. Afterward I will see his face; perhaps he will welcome me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: and you shall say, ‘Moreover your servant Jacob is behind us.’” For he thought, “I may appease him with the gift that goes ahead of me, and afterward I shall see his face; perhaps he will accept me.”

verses.rationale: Clarify the pronoun referent and preserve the contrast between the advancing gift and Jacob’s overnight stay.
verses.before: So the gift passed on ahead of him, and he himself spent that night in the camp.
verses.after: So the gift went ahead of Jacob, while he spent that night in the camp.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the gift passed on ahead of him, and he himself spent that night in the camp.

verses.rationale: Preserve the timing, exact family counts, place name, and the women’s enslaved status rather than presenting them as employees.
verses.before: That same night he rose and took his two wives, his two female servants, and his eleven children, and crossed the ford of the Jabbok.
verses.after: During the night Jacob got up, took his two wives, his two enslaved women, and his eleven children, and crossed the ford of the Jabbok.
verses.tsw_comparator: That same night he rose and took his two wives, his two female servants, and his eleven children, and crossed the ford of the Jabbok.

verses.rationale: Use a clear two-stage movement and retain that Jacob causes both his family and property to cross.
verses.before: He took them and sent them across the stream, and likewise sent across what was his.
verses.after: He took them across the stream, then sent all his possessions across.
verses.tsw_comparator: He took them and sent them across the stream, and likewise sent across what was his.

verses.rationale: Retain the abrupt isolation, the unidentified man, and the duration without prematurely identifying Jacob’s opponent.
verses.before: Jacob was left alone; and a man wrestled with him until the breaking of the day.
verses.after: Jacob was left alone, and a man wrestled with him until dawn.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Jacob was left alone; and a man wrestled with him until the breaking of the day.

verses.rationale: Resolve the otherwise confusing pronouns from the narrative sequence while preserving the opponent’s failure, touch, injury, and ongoing struggle.
verses.before: When he saw that he did not prevail against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh; and Jacob’s thigh was put out of joint as he wrestled with him.
verses.after: When the man saw that he could not overcome Jacob, he touched Jacob’s hip socket, dislocating it as they wrestled.
verses.tsw_comparator: When he saw that he did not prevail against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh; and Jacob’s thigh was put out of joint as he wrestled with him.

verses.rationale: Name the alternating speakers for oral comprehension and keep the dawn, refusal, and demanded blessing.
verses.before: Then he said, “Let me go, for the day is breaking.” But he said, “I will not let you go, unless you bless me.”
verses.after: The man said, “Let me go, because dawn is breaking.” Jacob answered, “I will not let you go unless you bless me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he said, “Let me go, for the day is breaking.” But he said, “I will not let you go, unless you bless me.”

verses.rationale: Keep the question and answer spare while making speaker movement immediately audible.
verses.before: And he said to him, “What is your name?” And he said, “Jacob.”
verses.after: The man asked him, “What is your name?” “Jacob,” he answered.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to him, “What is your name?” And he said, “Jacob.”

verses.rationale: Preserve the new name, its struggle word association, both divine and human opponents, and the consequential claim of prevailing.
verses.before: Then he said, “Your name will no longer be called Jacob, but Israel, for you have striven with God and with humans, and have prevailed.”
verses.after: The man said, “Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel, because you have struggled with God and with people and have prevailed.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he said, “Your name shall no longer be called Jacob, but Israel, for you have striven with God and with humans, and have prevailed.”

verses.rationale: Keep the unanswered request and place of blessing while naming the speakers without identifying the man beyond the text.
verses.before: Then Jacob asked him, “Please tell me your name.” But he said, “Why is it that you ask my name?” And there he blessed him.
verses.after: Jacob replied, “Please tell me your name.” But the man said, “Why do you ask my name?” Then he blessed Jacob there.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Jacob asked him, “Please tell me your name.” But he said, “Why is it that you ask my name?” And there he blessed him.

verses.rationale: Preserve Jacob’s own identification, the Peniel/face association, and the surprising survival claim.
verses.before: So Jacob called the name of the place Peniel, saying, “For I have seen God face to face, and yet my life is preserved.”
verses.after: Jacob named the place Peniel, saying, “I have seen God face to face, yet my life has been spared.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So Jacob called the name of the place Peniel, saying, “For I have seen God face to face, and yet my life is preserved.”

verses.rationale: Keep the sunrise image, the alternate place-name form, and the lasting bodily consequence in direct English.
verses.before: The sun rose upon him as he passed Penuel, limping because of his thigh.
verses.after: The sun rose over Jacob as he passed Penuel, and he was limping because of his hip.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sun rose upon him as he passed Penuel, limping because of his thigh.

verses.rationale: Retain the narrator’s later community perspective, bodily detail, dietary practice, and causal connection while avoiding a false anatomical precision.
verses.before: So to this day the Israelites do not eat the sinew of the thigh that is on the hollow of the thigh, because he touched the hollow of Jacob’s thigh at the sinew.
verses.after: That is why, to this day, the Israelites do not eat the sinew attached to the hip socket: the man touched Jacob’s hip socket at that sinew.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore to this day the Israelites do not eat the sinew of the thigh that is on the hollow of the thigh, because he touched the hollow of Jacob’s thigh at the sinew.

verses.rationale: Streamline the seeing formula while retaining the alarming number, named mothers, and the women’s enslaved status.
verses.before: Then Jacob lifted up his eyes and looked, and look, Esau was coming, and with him four hundred men. So he divided the children among Leah and Rachel and the two female servants.
verses.after: Jacob looked up and saw Esau approaching with four hundred men. He divided the children among Leah, Rachel, and the two enslaved women.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Jacob lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, Esau was coming, and with him four hundred men. So he divided the children among Leah and Rachel and the two female servants.

verses.rationale: Make the three-tier order unmistakable without supplying a motive the narrator does not state.
verses.before: He put the female servants and their children first, then Leah and her children, and Rachel and Joseph last of all.
verses.after: He placed the enslaved women and their children in front, Leah and her children behind them, and Rachel and Joseph last.
verses.tsw_comparator: He put the female servants and their children first, then Leah and her children, and Rachel and Joseph last of all.

verses.rationale: Preserve Jacob’s movement to the front, the exact repeated obeisance, and the brother relationship.
verses.before: And he himself went on before them, bowing himself to the ground seven times until he came near to his brother.
verses.after: Jacob himself went ahead of them, bowing to the ground seven times as he approached his brother.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he himself went on before them, bowing himself to the ground seven times until he came near to his brother.

verses.rationale: Keep Esau as the active reconciler, retain the affectionate sequence and mutual weeping, and flag the marked Hebrew word for kissed in a note.
verses.before: Yet Esau ran to meet him and embraced him and fell upon his neck and kissed him, and they wept.
verses.after: But Esau ran to meet Jacob, embraced him, fell on his neck, and kissed him. Then they both wept.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Esau ran to meet him and embraced him and fell upon his neck and kissed him, and they wept.

verses.rationale: Clarify speaker changes and the idiomatic question while preserving Jacob’s language of divine grace and deference.
verses.before: Then Esau lifted up his eyes and saw the women and children and said, “Who are these with you?” Jacob said, “The children whom God has graciously given your servant.”
verses.after: Esau looked up and saw the women and children. “Who are these people with you?” he asked. Jacob answered, “The children God has graciously given your servant.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Esau lifted up his eyes and saw the women and children and said, “Who are these with you?” Jacob said, “The children whom God has graciously given your servant.”

verses.rationale: Retain the family-unit action while naming the women’s status rather than reducing them to generic attendants.
verses.before: Then the female servants came near, they and their children, and bowed down.
verses.after: The enslaved women approached with their children, and together they bowed down.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the female servants came near, they and their children, and bowed down.

verses.rationale: Keep the source’s noteworthy Joseph-before-Rachel order and the repeated approach and bow.
verses.before: Leah likewise and her children came near and bowed down. And afterward Joseph and Rachel came near, and they bowed down.
verses.after: Leah and her children also approached and bowed down. After them Joseph and Rachel approached and bowed down.
verses.tsw_comparator: Leah likewise and her children came near and bowed down. And afterward Joseph and Rachel came near, and they bowed down.

verses.rationale: Render the idiomatic ownership question as purpose while preserving the camp motif and Jacob’s deferential aim.
verses.before: Esau said, “What do you mean by all this company that I met?” Jacob answered, “To find favor in the sight of my lord.”
verses.after: Esau asked, “What was the purpose of that entire camp I met?” Jacob answered, “To gain my lord’s favor.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And Esau said, “What do you mean by all this company that I met?” Jacob answered, “To find favor in the sight of my lord.”

verses.rationale: Retain Esau’s sufficiency, affectionate brother address, and refusal of the gift.
verses.before: Yet Esau said, “I have enough, my brother. Keep what belongs to you.”
verses.after: But Esau said, “I already have plenty, my brother. Keep what is yours.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But Esau said, “I have enough, my brother. Keep what belongs to you.”

verses.rationale: Preserve the repeated face language that links the reconciliation with Peniel and keep Jacob’s interpretation in his own voice.
verses.before: Jacob said, “No, please. If now I have found favor in your sight, then accept my gift from my hand. For to see your face is like seeing the face of God, since you have received me favorably.
verses.after: Jacob replied, “No, please. If I have found favor with you, accept this gift from me. Seeing your face is like seeing the face of God, because you have received me favorably.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jacob said, “No, please. If now I have found favor in your sight, then accept my gift from my hand. For to see your face is like seeing the face of God, since you have received me favorably.

verses.rationale: Retain Jacob’s striking word blessing and his claim to have everything, distinct from Esau’s plenty, without claiming the gift reverses chapter 27.
verses.before: Please accept my blessing that has been brought to you, because God has dealt graciously with me and because I have enough.” Thus he urged him, and he accepted.
verses.after: Please accept the blessing I brought you, because God has been gracious to me and I have everything.” Jacob kept urging him until Esau accepted it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Please accept my blessing that has been brought to you, because God has dealt graciously with me and because I have enough.” Thus he urged him, and he accepted.

verses.rationale: Choose alongside for the spatial phrase while preserving Esau’s offer of a shared journey; note the phrase can mean in front of you.
verses.before: Then Esau said, “Let us journey on our way, and I will go before you.”
verses.after: Then Esau said, “Let us set out together. I will travel alongside you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Esau said, “Let us journey on our way, and I will go before you.”

verses.rationale: Clarify Jacob’s care responsibility and preserve the vulnerable children, nursing animals, one-day limit, and total danger.
verses.before: Yet Jacob said to him, “My lord knows that the children are frail, and that the nursing flocks and herds are a care to me. If they are driven hard for even one day, all the flocks will die.
verses.after: Jacob answered, “My lord knows that the children are frail and that I am responsible for nursing flocks and herds. If they are driven hard for even one day, all the animals will die.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Jacob said to him, “My lord knows that the children are frail, and that the nursing flocks and herds are a care to me. If they are driven hard for even one day, all the flocks will die.

verses.rationale: Render the pace idiom naturally and retain Jacob’s stated destination without harmonizing it with his next move to Succoth.
verses.before: Let my lord pass on before his servant, and I will lead on slowly, according to the pace of the livestock that are before me and according to the pace of the children, until I come to my lord in Seir.”
verses.after: Please let my lord go on ahead of his servant. I will move at a gentle pace, according to the livestock and children before me, until I reach my lord in Seir.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Let my lord pass on before his servant, and I will lead on slowly, according to the pace of the livestock that are before me and according to the pace of the children, until I come to my lord in Seir.”

verses.rationale: Clarify the elliptical refusal without adding suspicion and preserve Esau’s offer and Jacob’s deferential response.
verses.before: So Esau said, “Let me leave with you some of the people who are with me.” But he said, “Why should that be? Let me only find favor in the sight of my lord.”
verses.after: Esau said, “Then let me leave some of my people with you.” Jacob answered, “There is no need. Just let me remain in my lord’s favor.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So Esau said, “Let me leave with you some of the people who are with me.” But he said, “Why should that be? Let me only find favor in the sight of my lord.”

verses.rationale: Use direct movement language while retaining the exact day and destination.
verses.before: So Esau returned that day on his way to Seir.
verses.after: That same day Esau started back toward Seir.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Esau returned that day on his way to Seir.

verses.rationale: Preserve the house/shelters contrast and the Succoth word association in natural narrative order.
verses.before: Yet Jacob journeyed to Succoth, and built himself a house and made shelters for his livestock. Therefore the name of the place is called Succoth.
verses.after: Jacob traveled to Succoth, built a house for himself, and made shelters for his livestock. That is why the place was named Succoth.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Jacob journeyed to Succoth, and built himself a house and made shelters for his livestock. Therefore the name of the place is called Succoth.

verses.rationale: Follow the adverbial reading safely while retaining the possible place-name reading Salem in a note.
verses.before: Then Jacob came safely to the city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, when he came from Paddan-aram, and he camped before the city.
verses.after: After returning from Paddan-aram, Jacob arrived safely at the city of Shechem in the land of Canaan and camped near the city.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Jacob came safely to the city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, when he came from Paddan-aram, and he camped before the city.

verses.rationale: Retain the unknown ancient monetary unit rather than disguising it as a known coin or weight; keep seller, relationship, field, and amount.
verses.before: And from the sons of Hamor, Shechem’s father, he bought for one hundred pieces of money the portion of the field where he had pitched his tent.
verses.after: He bought the field where he had pitched his tent from the sons of Hamor, Shechem’s father, for one hundred qesitahs.
verses.tsw_comparator: And from the sons of Hamor, Shechem’s father, he bought for one hundred pieces of money the portion of the field where he had pitched his tent.

verses.rationale: Preserve the Hebrew altar name for literary continuity and explain its meaning selectively in vocabulary.
verses.before: There he erected an altar and called it El-Elohe-Israel.
verses.after: There Jacob set up an altar and named it El-Elohe-Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: There he erected an altar and called it El-Elohe-Israel.

verses.rationale: Keep Dinah’s maternal identity and ordinary social purpose clear without making her action responsible for what follows.
verses.before: Now Dinah, the daughter of Leah, whom she had borne to Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land.
verses.after: Dinah, the daughter Leah had borne to Jacob, went out to visit the women of the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now Dinah, the daughter of Leah, whom she had borne to Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land.

verses.rationale: Name the sexual violence directly from the sequence of taking, lying with, and afflicting; retain Shechem’s identity and power without euphemizing Dinah’s harm.
verses.before: Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, the prince of the land, saw her. He took her and lay with her and humiliated her.
verses.after: Shechem son of Hamor the Hivite, a ruler of the land, saw her, seized her, raped her, and humiliated her.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, the prince of the land, saw her. He took her and lay with her and humiliated her.

verses.rationale: Keep Shechem’s later attachment and tenderness in sequence without allowing them to erase the preceding rape or supplying Dinah’s response.
verses.before: Yet his soul clung to Dinah the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the young woman and spoke tenderly to her.
